paper.title: Structure and Optimality of Myopic Policy in Opportunistic Access with Noisy Observations

settings.name_in_paper: Multichannel opportunistic access with i.i.d. Gilbert-Elliot channels and noisy observations (restless bandit)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Restless Markov bandit / POMDP with known Markov model; markovian environments are out of scope in v0.5 and the objective is Bayes-optimal control rather than learning.
unmapped: Each arm is a two-state Markov chain (Gilbert-Elliot) with transition probabilities p_ij, identical across arms
Channel state observed through a detector with false alarm prob epsilon and miss detection prob delta; only ACK/NAK observed
Objective is maximizing expected total reward over T slots given an initial belief vector (POMDP)
settings.definition_quote: Assume that there are $N$ independent and stochastically identical Gilbert-Elliot channels... In each time slot, a user chooses one of the $N$ channels to sense and subsequently access if the chosen channel is sensed to be in the good state. Sensing is subject to errors

conditions: epsilon < p10*p01/(p11*p00) if p11 >= p01; epsilon < p00*p11/(p01*p10) if p11 < p01
initial belief values bounded between p01 and p11

source.label: thm:optimality
source.quote: For $N=2$, the myopic policy is optimal when $\epsilon<\frac{p_{10}p_{01}}{p_{11}p_{00}}$ for positively correlated channels ($p_{11}\ge p_{01}$) and $\epsilon<\frac{p_{00}p_{11}}{p_{01}p_{10}}$ for negatively correlated channels ($p_{11}< p_{01}$) when the initial belief values are bounded between $p_{01}$ and $p_{11}$.

results.notes: Optimality statement encoded as zero gap in expected total reward vs the optimal POMDP policy over horizon T. Not a learning regret bound. Policy only needs the order of p11 and p01.
